extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks requiring college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It contains 11.5K multimodal questions across six disciplines, 30 subjects, and many heterogeneous image types.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was built in three stages: first, the authors selected 30 subjects from six disciplines based on common university majors and the presence of visual inputs; second, they recruited over 50 university students (including co-authors) as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources and to create new questions when necessary; third, the authors cleaned duplicates, checked format/typos, and assigned difficulty levels, excluding about 10% of very easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with the design criteria, were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions sourced from major textbooks and online resources, with some new questions created by annotators; the benchmark also draws from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, online sources, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The benchmark questions were manually collected by over 50 university students (including coauthors) specializing in the relevant majors. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, and created new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations and to avoid questions with immediately available answers. Data quality control included duplicate removal, format and typo checking by co-authors, and difficulty categorization.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control was performed through duplicate detection using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, author review of suspected duplicates, format and typo checking, and final difficulty categorization. No inter-annotator agreement metrics are reported.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including coauthors, specializing in the relevant majors; later, 90 college senior students were used as human experts for validation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases, and GPT-4V often exhibits a bias towards perceptual error.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU has limitations despite its comprehensive nature; the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. The benchmark also combines multiple-choice with concise open-ended questions to address challenges associated with evaluating open-ended responses.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MMMU is presented as a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating the capabilities of LMMs in the context of Expert AGI, assessing both basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities across various professional domains.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data Quality Control: duplicate problems were identified using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, then reviewed and eliminated; format and typo checking were performed; approximately 10% of very easy problems were excluded.
